curriculum.title: Curriculum Structure — Chinese Language & Literature, Creative Writing & Digital Humanities
content: **Programme Overview**: JS7101 Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Chinese offers three distinct streams — **Chinese Language & Literature**, **Creative Writing**, and **Digital Humanities**. Students select one stream after Year 1, with flexibility to take electives from other streams.

**Year 1 — Foundation Year**: Core courses include **Introduction to Chinese Literature**, **Modern Chinese Language**, **Classical Chinese Prose**, and **University English**. Students also complete Lingnan’s **Liberal Arts Core** (e.g., Critical Thinking, Ethics).

**Year 2 — Stream Selection & Specialisation**: Students choose their stream. Chinese Language & Literature stream covers **Classical Poetry**, **Chinese Linguistics**, and **Literary Criticism**. Creative Writing stream offers **Fiction Writing**, **Poetry Workshop**, and **Scriptwriting**. Digital Humanities stream includes **Digital Text Analysis**, **Data Visualisation for Humanities**, and **Computational Literary Studies**.

**Year 3 — Advanced Study & Exchange**: Advanced courses such as **Chinese Literary History**, **Creative Non-fiction**, and **Digital Publishing**. All students are encouraged to participate in a **one-semester exchange** at one of Lingnan’s 200+ partner universities. A **Capstone Project** begins in this year.

**Year 4 — Capstone & Career Preparation**: Students complete a **Capstone Project** (e.g., a creative writing portfolio, a digital humanities research paper, or a literary thesis). Professional development workshops and **internship placements** in media, publishing, and cultural organisations are available.

**Language & Liberal Arts Requirement**: All students must complete **English language enhancement** courses and a **Chinese language proficiency** assessment. Lingnan’s liberal arts curriculum includes **Service-Learning** and **Community Engagement** courses.

career.title: Career Prospects — From Literature to Digital Media
content: **Publishing & Editorial**: Graduates work as **editors**, **proofreaders**, and **publishing managers** at major Hong Kong publishers such as **Joint Publishing** and **Commercial Press**. The Creative Writing stream provides a strong portfolio for literary careers.

**Media & Journalism**: Alumni enter roles as **journalists**, **scriptwriters**, and **content creators** for media outlets like **TVB**, **Now TV**, and **Ming Pao**. The Digital Humanities stream equips students with data storytelling skills.

**Education & Academia**: Many graduates become **Chinese language teachers** in secondary schools or pursue **MPhil/PhD** programmes in Chinese literature or digital humanities at local and overseas universities.

**Cultural & Creative Industries**: Career paths include **museum curator**, **cultural programme officer**, and **arts administrator** at organisations like **Hong Kong Arts Development Council** and **M+ Museum**.
**Digital Content & Marketing**: Digital Humanities graduates are sought after for roles in **digital marketing**, **UX writing**, and **social media management** in agencies and corporations.
**Government & NGOs**: Graduates join the **Hong Kong Government** as **Executive Officers** or work in **NGOs** focusing on cultural preservation and community education.

campus.title: Campus Life — Liberal Arts in Tuen Mun
content: **Residential Halls**: All Lingnan students are required to live in **residential halls** for at least one year. Halls host cultural nights, writing workshops, and literary salons, fostering a close-knit community.

**Small Class Sizes**: With an average class size of **20-30 students**, Chinese programme students receive personalised attention from professors. Tutorials and seminars encourage deep discussion of texts and creative works.

**Library & Digital Lab**: The **Lingnan University Library** houses extensive Chinese literature collections and a **Digital Humanities Lab** equipped with text-mining software and VR tools for literary analysis.

**Exchange & Global Learning**: Lingnan has **over 200 partner universities** in 40+ countries. Chinese programme students frequently exchange to **Peking University**, **National Taiwan University**, or **University of California** for a semester.

**Cultural Activities on Campus**: The **Chinese Cultural Centre** organises poetry readings, calligraphy workshops, and film screenings. The annual **Lingnan Arts Festival** showcases student creative works.
**Location & Transport**: The campus is located in **Tuen Mun**, with direct bus and MTR connections to Kowloon and Hong Kong Island. The scenic seaside location offers a quiet environment for study.

competitiveness.title: Competitiveness Analysis — How to Secure Your Place
content: **Overall Level**: High (★★★★☆)
**Admission Score (2025)**: Median score **25.845** and Lower Quartile **25.27** (Best 5 subjects). This places JS7101 among the more competitive arts programmes at Lingnan.

**Demand vs. Places**: In 2025, **280 Band A applicants** and **120 Band B applicants** competed for just **55 first-year places**. Total applicants reached **650**, giving a Band A-to-place ratio of approximately **5:1**.

**Subject Requirements**: Strong performance in **Chinese Language** is critical (Median **5**, LQ **4**). English and Mathematics at **Level 3** are typical. Electives should be at **Level 4** or above to be competitive.
**No Interview Required**: Admission is purely based on HKDSE scores. This means your **Best 5 subjects** must be maximised — every grade counts directly.

**Liberal Arts Advantage**: Lingnan’s liberal arts focus means the programme values **broad academic exposure**. Students with strong results in humanities electives (e.g., History, Literature) have an edge.

content: **Dr. Leung Ping-kwan (也斯)**: Renowned Hong Kong poet, novelist, and cultural critic. He taught at Lingnan University and was a key figure in modern Chinese literature. (Posthumous recognition; associated with Lingnan’s Chinese programme.)
**Ms. Wong Wai-yin (黃慧妍)**: Award-winning writer and editor at **Ming Pao Weekly**. She graduated from Lingnan’s Chinese programme and has published several short story collections.

**Dr. Lee Hiu-man (李曉雯)**: Assistant Professor of Chinese Literature at **Hong Kong Baptist University**. She completed her BA in Chinese at Lingnan and later earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong.

scholarships.title: Scholarships & Financial Support — Recognising Excellence
content: **Lingnan University Entrance Scholarship**: Awarded to students with outstanding HKDSE results (e.g., score above **28 in Best 5**). Covers full or half tuition fees for the first year.
**Faculty of Arts Dean’s Scholarship**: For top-performing Year 1 students in the Faculty of Arts, including Chinese programme students. Provides up to **HK$20,000** per year.
**Dr. Lau Chor Tak Scholarship for Chinese Studies**: Specifically for Chinese programme students with strong academic records and a passion for Chinese literature. Value: **HK$15,000**.
**Creative Writing Prize**: Annual competition for Creative Writing stream students. Winners receive **HK$5,000** and publication opportunities in Lingnan’s literary magazine.
**Exchange Scholarship**: Students going on exchange can apply for the **Lingnan Global Scholarship** (up to **HK$30,000**) to cover travel and living expenses.
**Service-Learning Bursary**: For students engaged in community projects related to Chinese language and culture. Provides **HK$10,000** to support project costs.

tips.title: Ace Sir's JS7101 Strategy — 9 Actionable Tips
content: **1. Prioritise Chinese Language — Target Level 5 or Above**
- The median Chinese grade for 2025 was **Level 5**, and the LQ was **Level 4**. Aim for **Level 5** to be safe. Focus on classical Chinese texts and essay writing skills.
- Use past papers and practice timed essays. Join a Chinese literature study group to deepen analysis.
**2. Strengthen Your Electives — Two Level 4s Are Essential**
- Elective 1 median was **Level 4** and Elective 2 median was **Level 4** (LQ 3). Choose electives like **Chinese Literature**, **History**, or **Geography** that complement the programme.
- Aim for **Level 5** in at least one elective to boost your Best 5 score above the median.
**3. Don’t Neglect English — Level 3 Is the Floor**
- English median was **Level 3**. While not as competitive as Chinese, a **Level 4** in English can give you an edge over other applicants with similar scores.
- Practice reading comprehension and writing argumentative essays. Use Lingnan’s English enhancement resources if admitted.
**4. Mathematics at Level 3 Is Sufficient — Focus Elsewhere**
- Mathematics median was **Level 3**. Don’t spend excessive time on Maths if you are weaker — invest that time in Chinese and electives where higher grades matter more.
- Ensure you meet the **Level 3** minimum; a **Level 4** is a bonus but not necessary.
**5. Citizenship and Social Development — Attained Is Enough**
- The median and LQ for Citizenship were both **Attained**. This subject is a pass/fail hurdle. Do not over-invest; just ensure you pass.
- Focus your revision energy on the five subjects that count in your Best 5 calculation.
**6. Build a Portfolio for Creative Writing or Digital Humanities**
- If you are interested in the **Creative Writing** stream, start a blog or submit short stories to school magazines. A portfolio can strengthen your application and prepare you for the stream.
- For **Digital Humanities**, learn basic Python or data visualisation tools (e.g., Tableau) during summer. This shows genuine interest.
**7. Use Liberal Arts to Your Advantage — Show Breadth**

- Lingnan values whole-person education. In your personal statement (if required), highlight your involvement in **community service**, **cultural activities**, or **debate**. This aligns with the liberal arts ethos.
- Mention any reading habits, literary awards, or volunteer teaching of Chinese.
**8. Apply Early in Band A — 280 Band A Applicants in 2025**
- With **280 Band A applicants** for 55 places, being in Band A is crucial. Place JS7101 as your **first or second choice** in Band A to maximise your chance.
- Band B had only **120 applicants**, but most offers go to Band A. Don’t rely on Band B.
**9. Target a Best 5 Score of 26+ for Safety**
- The median score was **25.845** and LQ was **25.27**. Aim for **26 points** or higher to be comfortably above the median. Calculate your predicted score using your school’s mock exam results.
- If your predicted score is below 25, consider a backup programme with lower requirements.

curriculum.title: 課程結構 — 中國語言與文學、創意寫作及數字人文
content: **課程概覽**：JS7101 中文(榮譽)文學士提供三個專修方向——**中國語言與文學**、**創意寫作**及**數字人文**。學生在第一年後選擇專修，並可選修其他方向的科目。
**第一年 — 基礎年**：核心課程包括**中國文學導論**、**現代中國語言**、**古典散文**及**大學英語**。學生亦須完成嶺南大學的**博雅教育核心課程**（如批判思考、倫理學）。
**第二年 — 專修選擇與深化**：學生選擇專修。中國語言與文學專修涵蓋**古典詩歌**、**中國語言學**及**文學批評**。創意寫作專修提供**小說創作**、**詩歌工作坊**及**劇本寫作**。數字人文專修包括**數位文本分析**、**人文學數據可視化**及**計算文學研究**。
**第三年 — 高階學習與交流**：高階課程如**中國文學史**、**創意非虛構寫作**及**數位出版**。鼓勵所有學生參加為期一學期的**交換計劃**，前往嶺南大學全球200多所合作院校。**頂點項目**於本學年開始。
**第四年 — 頂點項目與職業準備**：學生完成**頂點項目**（如創意寫作作品集、數字人文研究論文或文學論文）。提供專業發展工作坊及**實習機會**，涵蓋媒體、出版及文化機構。
**語言與博雅要求**：所有學生須完成**英語強化課程**及**中文能力評核**。嶺南大學的博雅課程包括**服務研習**及**社區參與**科目。

career.title: 就業前景 — 從文學到數碼媒體
content: **出版與編輯**：畢業生任職**編輯**、**校對**及**出版經理**，於香港主要出版社如**三聯書店**及**商務印書館**工作。創意寫作專修為文學職業提供堅實的作品集。
**媒體與新聞**：校友擔任**記者**、**編劇**及**內容創作者**，服務於**無綫電視**、**Now TV**及**明報**等媒體。數字人文專修培養數據敘事技能。
**教育與學術**：許多畢業生成為中學**中文教師**，或在本地及海外大學攻讀中國文學或數字人文的**哲學碩士/博士**課程。
**文化與創意產業**：職業路徑包括**博物館館長**、**文化節目主任**及**藝術行政人員**，任職於**香港藝術發展局**及**M+博物館**等機構。
**數碼內容與市場營銷**：數字人文畢業生在**數碼營銷**、**用戶體驗寫作**及**社交媒體管理**等職位中備受青睞，服務於廣告公司及企業。
**政府與非政府組織**：畢業生加入**香港政府**擔任**行政主任**，或在專注文化保育及社區教育的**非政府組織**工作。

campus.title: 校園生活 — 屯門的博雅教育
content: **住宿書院**：所有嶺南學生須至少入住**住宿書院**一年。書院舉辦文化之夜、寫作工作坊及文學沙龍，培養緊密的社群關係。
**小班教學**：中文課程平均每班**20至30名學生**，教授提供個人化指導。導修課及研討會鼓勵深入討論文本及創意作品。
**圖書館與數碼實驗室**：**嶺南大學圖書館**收藏豐富的中國文學資料，並設有**數字人文實驗室**，配備文本挖掘軟件及虛擬實境工具，用於文學分析。
**交換與全球學習**：嶺南大學與全球40多個國家的**超過200所合作院校**建立聯繫。中文課程學生常前往**北京大學**、**國立台灣大學**或**加州大學**進行一學期交換。
**校園文化活動**：**中國文化中心**舉辦詩歌朗誦會、書法工作坊及電影放映會。年度**嶺南藝術節**展示學生的創意作品。
**地理位置與交通**：校園位於**屯門**，設有直達巴士及港鐵連接九龍及香港島。海濱環境寧靜，適合學習。

competitiveness.title: 競爭力分析 — 如何確保錄取
content: **2025年入學分數**：中位數 **25.845** 分，下四分位數 **25.27** 分（最佳五科）。這使 JS7101 成為嶺南大學競爭較激烈的文學課程之一。
**需求與學額**：2025年，**280名Band A申請者**及**120名Band B申請者**競爭僅**55個一年級學額**。總申請人數達**650人**，Band A與學額比例約為**5:1**。
**科目要求**：**中文科**成績至關重要（中位數**5級**，下四分位數**4級**）。英文及數學達**3級**為典型。選修科須達**4級**或以上才具競爭力。
**無需面試**：錄取完全基於香港中學文憑考試成績。因此，你的**最佳五科**必須最大化——每一分都直接影響結果。
**博雅教育優勢**：嶺南大學的博雅教育方針重視**廣泛的學術接觸**。在人文學科選修科（如歷史、文學）成績優異的學生更具優勢。

alumni.title: 知名校友 — 嶺南中文畢業生發揮影響力
content: **也斯博士 (Leung Ping-kwan)**：香港著名詩人、小說家及文化評論家。他曾於嶺南大學任教，是現代中國文學的關鍵人物。（追認；與嶺南中文課程相關。）
**黃慧妍女士 (Wong Wai-yin)**：獲獎作家及《明報周刊》編輯。她畢業於嶺南大學中文課程，已出版多部短篇小說集。
**陳國強先生 (Chan Kwok-keung)**：**三聯書店（香港）** 高級編輯。他負責中國文學及人文學科出版。嶺南大學中文課程畢業生。
**李曉雯博士 (Lee Hiu-man)**：**香港浸會大學**中國文學助理教授。她在嶺南大學獲得中文學士學位，其後於香港大學取得博士學位。
**鄭嘉欣女士 (Cheng Ka-yan)**：**香港藝術發展局**文化節目主任。她管理文學資助及社區藝術項目。嶺南大學中文課程畢業生。
**曾顯威先生 (Tsang Hin-wai)**：**香港商業電台**數碼內容經理。他運用數字人文技能製作多媒體文學內容。嶺南大學中文課程畢業生。

scholarships.title: 獎學金與財政支援 — 表彰卓越
content: **嶺南大學入學獎學金**：頒予香港中學文憑考試成績優異的學生（如最佳五科**28分以上**）。涵蓋首年全額或半額學費。
**文學院院長獎學金**：頒予文學院（包括中文課程）一年級成績最優秀的學生。每年最高**20,000港元**。
**Dr. Lau Chor Tak 中國研究獎學金**：專為中文課程成績優異及對中國文學充滿熱誠的學生而設。金額**15,000港元**。
**創意寫作獎**：創意寫作專修學生的年度比賽。得獎者獲**5,000港元**及在嶺南大學文學雜誌發表的機會。
**交換獎學金**：參加交換計劃的學生可申請**嶺南環球獎學金**（最高**30,000港元**），以支付旅費及生活開支。
**服務研習助學金**：資助參與中文語言及文化相關社區項目的學生。提供**10,000港元**支持項目開支。

tips.title: Ace Sir JS7101 攻略 — 9 個實用貼士
content: **1. 優先處理中文科 — 目標5級或以上**
- 2025年中位數為**5級**，下四分位數為**4級**。以**5級**為目標以策安全。專注於古典中文文本及作文技巧。
- 使用歷屆試題並練習限時作文。加入中文文學研習小組以深化分析能力。
**2. 強化選修科 — 兩個4級是必須的**
- 選修科1中位數為**4級**，選修科2中位數為**4級**（下四分位數3級）。選擇與課程互補的選修科，如**中國文學**、**歷史**或**地理**。
- 目標在至少一個選修科取得**5級**，以將最佳五科分數提升至中位數以上。
**3. 不要忽視英文 — 3級是底線**
- 英文中位數為**3級**。雖然競爭不如中文激烈，但**4級**的英文成績可讓你在分數相近的申請者中脫穎而出。
- 練習閱讀理解及議論文寫作。如獲錄取，可使用嶺南大學的英語強化資源。
**4. 數學3級已足夠 — 專注其他科目**
- 數學中位數為**3級**。如果你數學較弱，不要花過多時間——將時間投入中文及選修科，這些科目的高分更為重要。
- 確保達到**3級**最低要求；**4級**是加分項，但非必要。
**5. 公民與社會發展科 — 達標即可**
- 中位數及下四分位數均為**達標**。此科為合格與否的門檻。不要過度投入；確保合格即可。
- 將溫習精力集中於計入最佳五科的五個科目。
**6. 為創意寫作或數字人文建立作品集**
- 如果你對**創意寫作**專修感興趣，開始寫博客或向校刊投稿短篇小說。作品集可強化你的申請，並為專修做好準備。
- 對於**數字人文**，在暑假期間學習基礎Python或數據可視化工具（如Tableau）。這顯示你真實的興趣。
**7. 善用博雅教育優勢 — 展現廣度**
- 嶺南大學重視全人教育。在個人陳述（如有要求）中，強調你參與**社區服務**、**文化活動**或**辯論**的經歷。這與博雅教育理念一致。
- 提及你的閱讀習慣、文學獎項或義務教授中文的經驗。
**8. 盡早於Band A申請 — 2025年有280名Band A申請者**
- 2025年有**280名Band A申請者**競爭55個學額，身處Band A至關重要。將JS7101列為Band A的**第一或第二志願**以最大化機會。
- Band B僅有**120名申請者**，但大多數錄取通知發給Band A。不要依賴Band B。
**9. 以最佳五科26分以上為安全目標**
- 中位數為**25.845分**，下四分位數為**25.27分**。目標取得**26分或以上**，以穩居中位數之上。使用學校模擬考試成績計算預測分數。
- 如果你的預測分數低於25分，考慮一個要求較低的備選課程。

nameEn: Bachelor of Liberal Arts (Hons) in Global Development and Sustainability
nameZh: 環球可持續發展(榮譽)博雅學士

curriculum.title: Curriculum Structure
content: **Programme Overview**: JS7123 Bachelor of Liberal Arts (Hons) in Global Development and Sustainability is a 4-year interdisciplinary programme offered by the School of Interdisciplinary Studies. It focuses on sustainable development through four concentrations: Policy & Institutions, Culture & Community, Business & Economy, and Human-Environment Interactions.

**Year 1**: Students take foundational courses in liberal arts, including critical thinking, writing, and introductory modules on global development and sustainability. Core courses cover environmental science basics, social theory, and economic principles.

**Year 2**: Students deepen their understanding with intermediate courses such as 'Sustainable Development Policy', 'Cultural Ecology', and 'Global Political Economy'. They also select their concentration and begin specialized electives.

**Year 3**: Advanced coursework includes 'Environmental Governance', 'Community-Based Conservation', and 'Sustainable Business Models'. Students may participate in a capstone project or internship related to their concentration.

**Year 4**: The final year features a research thesis or applied project, plus advanced seminars. Students also have opportunities for exchange programmes at partner universities worldwide, leveraging Lingnan's strong global network.

**Concentration Options**: The four concentrations allow tailored study: Policy & Institutions (focus on governance and law), Culture & Community (focus on social and cultural dynamics), Business & Economy (focus on sustainable enterprise), and Human-Environment Interactions (focus on ecological systems and resource management).

career.title: Career Prospects
content: **Diverse Sectors**: Graduates are prepared for careers in government agencies, NGOs, international organizations, corporate sustainability departments, and environmental consultancies. The interdisciplinary nature of the programme opens doors to policy analysis, community development, sustainable finance, and conservation management.

**Policy & Institutions Track**: Typical roles include policy analyst, legislative assistant, or public affairs officer in government bodies like the Hong Kong Environmental Protection Department or the Development Bureau.

**Culture & Community Track**: Graduates often work as community development officers, cultural programme managers, or social impact researchers for NGOs such as Oxfam Hong Kong or local community foundations.
**Business & Economy Track**: Career paths include sustainability consultant, ESG analyst, or corporate social responsibility manager in firms like HSBC, Swire Group, or MTR Corporation.

**Human-Environment Interactions Track**: Opportunities include environmental scientist, conservation officer, or urban planner in organizations like the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) Hong Kong or the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department.

**Further Study**: Many graduates pursue master's degrees in sustainable development, public policy, environmental management, or international relations at top universities worldwide, including the University of Hong Kong, University of Cambridge, and London School of Economics.

campus.title: Campus Life
content: **Residential Experience**: Lingnan University requires all students to live in residential halls for at least one year, fostering a close-knit community. Halls offer study rooms, common areas, and organized activities that enhance peer learning and cultural exchange.

**Small Class Sizes**: With a low student-to-faculty ratio, classes typically have 20-30 students, allowing for personalized attention and interactive discussions. Professors are accessible and mentor students closely.

**Green Campus**: The Tuen Mun campus features lush gardens, a lake, and eco-friendly buildings. Students can participate in sustainability initiatives like the campus-wide recycling programme and organic farming projects.

**Exchange Opportunities**: Lingnan has over 200 partner universities in 40+ countries. Students in JS7123 can spend a semester or year abroad, with options in Europe, North America, Asia, and Australia, often with scholarships.

**Community Service**: The university emphasizes social responsibility through the 'Service-Learning' programme. Students engage in local and international community projects, such as environmental clean-ups in Tuen Mun or teaching in rural Cambodia.

**Student Societies**: Active clubs include the Sustainability Society, Debate Team, and Cultural Exchange Club. These groups organize events like eco-fairs, film screenings, and guest lectures from industry leaders.

competitiveness.title: Competitiveness Analysis
content: **Overall Level**: High (★★★★☆)

**Admission Scores**: The median HKDSE score for 2025 entry was 26.96 (Best 5 subjects), with a lower quartile of 26.07. This places JS7123 among the more competitive programmes at Lingnan, reflecting strong demand.

**Subject Requirements**: Strong performance in electives is critical: Elective 1 median was 5, and Elective 2 median was 4. Chinese and English medians were 4 and 3.5 respectively, while Citizenship and Social Development required only 'Attained'.

**Application Demand**: In 2025, there were 180 Band A applicants, 80 Band B applicants, and 420 total applicants for only 30 first-year places. This translates to a Band A-to-place ratio of 6:1, indicating high selectivity.
**No Interview**: The programme does not require an interview, so admission is purely based on HKDSE scores. This makes it essential to maximize your Best 5 subjects, especially electives.

**Trends**: The median score has remained stable around 26-27 over recent years, suggesting consistent competitiveness. Applicants with scores above 27 have a strong chance, while those at 26 should consider it a realistic target.

alumni.title: Notable Alumni

**Mr. Li Wai-ting (李偉霆先生)**: Sustainability Manager, MTR Corporation. A 2018 graduate, he oversees the company's carbon neutrality roadmap and has been featured in the 'Young Sustainability Leaders' list by the Hong Kong Institute of Planners.

scholarships.title: Scholarships and Financial Aid
content: **Lingnan University Entrance Scholarship**: Awarded to top HKDSE achievers (score 28+ in Best 5 subjects). Covers full or partial tuition for the first year, renewable based on academic performance. Approximately 10% of new students receive this.

**Global Development and Sustainability Programme Scholarship**: Specifically for JS7123 students with outstanding academic records (GPA 3.5+). Offers up to HK$50,000 per year for tuition and study-related expenses.

**Exchange Scholarship**: Supports students who participate in overseas exchange programmes. Covers airfare, accommodation, and living expenses up to HK$80,000 per semester. Over 60% of eligible students receive funding.

**Community Service Scholarship**: For students who demonstrate exceptional commitment to service-learning and community projects. Provides HK$20,000 annually and priority access to international volunteer placements.

**HKSAR Government Scholarship**: Available to local students with outstanding academic and extracurricular achievements. Valued at HK$40,000 per year, with a separate award for students with disabilities.

**Need-Based Financial Aid**: Lingnan offers means-tested grants and loans through the 'Lingnan Financial Assistance Scheme'. Covers up to full tuition and living costs for students from low-income families.

tips.title: Ace Sir's JS7123 Strategy — 9 Actionable Tips
content: **1. Prioritize Elective Subjects**

- Elective 1 median was 5 and Elective 2 median was 4 in 2025, so aim for Level 5 or above in at least one elective. Choose electives like Geography, Economics, or Biology that align with sustainability themes.
**2. Target a Best 5 Score of 27+**
- The median was 26.96, so a score of 27 or higher gives you a strong edge. Calculate your predicted Best 5 score early and focus on weak subjects.
**3. Excel in Chinese and English**

- Chinese median was 4 and English median was 3.5. Aim for Level 4 in both to stay competitive. Practice writing argumentative essays and reading comprehension for Chinese; for English, focus on vocabulary and critical analysis.
**4. Use Citizenship as a Baseline**
- Only 'Attained' is required for Citizenship and Social Development, so allocate minimal study time here. Use the saved time to boost your electives.
**5. Leverage Liberal Arts Strengths**
- Lingnan values critical thinking and interdisciplinary knowledge. In your personal statement (if required), highlight how your interests span policy, culture, business, and environment.
**6. Apply Early in JUPAS**
- With 180 Band A applicants for 30 places, Band A placement is crucial. Put JS7123 as your first or second choice in Band A to maximize chances.
**7. Consider the No-Interview Advantage**
- Since no interview is required, your HKDSE scores are the sole criterion. Focus entirely on exam preparation rather than interview practice.
**8. Research the Concentrations**

- Review the four concentrations and align your elective choices accordingly. For example, if you choose Business & Economy, take Economics and BAFS; for Human-Environment Interactions, take Geography and Biology.
**9. Plan for Exchange and Scholarships**
- Aim for a high GPA (3.5+) to qualify for programme-specific scholarships and exchange funding. Research partner universities early and prepare language requirements.

curriculum.title: 課程結構
content: **課程概覽**：JS7123 環球可持續發展(榮譽)博雅學士是一個為期四年的跨學科課程，由跨學科研究學院開設。課程聚焦可持續發展，提供四個專修方向：政策和機構、文化及社區、商業及經濟、人類與環境的互動。
**第一年**：學生修讀博雅教育基礎課程，包括批判性思考、寫作，以及環球可持續發展入門單元。核心課程涵蓋環境科學基礎、社會理論和經濟原理。
**第二年**：學生通過中級課程深化理解，例如「可持續發展政策」、「文化生態學」和「全球政治經濟學」。同時選擇專修方向並開始專業選修。
**第三年**：高級課程包括「環境治理」、「社區為本的保育」和「可持續商業模式」。學生可參與與專修相關的頂石項目或實習。
**第四年**：最後一年設有研究論文或應用項目，以及高級研討會。學生還有機會利用嶺南大學強大的全球網絡，到合作夥伴大學參加交流計劃。
**專修選擇**：四個專修方向提供量身定制的學習：政策和機構（聚焦治理與法律）、文化及社區（聚焦社會與文化動態）、商業及經濟（聚焦可持續企業）、人類與環境的互動（聚焦生態系統與資源管理）。

career.title: 就業前景
content: **多元行業**：畢業生可勝任政府機構、非政府組織、國際組織、企業可持續發展部門及環境顧問公司的工作。課程的跨學科性質為政策分析、社區發展、可持續金融和保育管理打開大門。
**政策和機構方向**：典型職位包括政策分析師、立法助理或公共事務主任，任職於香港環境保護署或發展局等政府部門。
**文化及社區方向**：畢業生常擔任社區發展主任、文化項目經理或社會影響研究員，服務於樂施會等非政府組織或本地社區基金會。
**商業及經濟方向**：職業路徑包括可持續發展顧問、ESG分析師或企業社會責任經理，任職於滙豐、太古集團或港鐵公司等企業。
**人類與環境的互動方向**：機會包括環境科學家、保育主任或城市規劃師，任職於世界自然基金會香港分會或漁農自然護理署等機構。
**深造進修**：許多畢業生在世界頂尖大學攻讀可持續發展、公共政策、環境管理或國際關係碩士學位，包括香港大學、劍橋大學和倫敦政治經濟學院。

campus.title: 校園生活
content: **住宿體驗**：嶺南大學要求所有學生至少住校一年，培養緊密的社群關係。宿舍設有自修室、公共空間和組織活動，促進同儕學習和文化交流。
**小班教學**：師生比例低，每班通常20-30人，提供個別關注和互動討論。教授平易近人，並密切指導學生。
**綠色校園**：屯門校園擁有茂盛花園、湖泊和環保建築。學生可參與可持續發展計劃，如校園回收計劃和有機耕種項目。
**交流機會**：嶺南大學與40多個國家的200多所夥伴大學合作。JS7123學生可到歐洲、北美、亞洲和澳洲交流一個學期或一年，通常有獎學金支持。
**社區服務**：大學通過「服務研習」計劃強調社會責任。學生參與本地和國際社區項目，例如屯門的環保清潔活動或柬埔寨鄉村教學。
**學生社團**：活躍的學會包括可持續發展學會、辯論隊和文化交流學會。這些團體舉辦生態展覽、電影放映和行業領袖講座等活動。

competitiveness.title: 競爭力分析
content: **入學分數**：2025年入學的HKDSE中位數為26.96分（最佳5科），下四分位數為26.07分。這使JS7123成為嶺南大學競爭較激烈的課程之一，反映需求強勁。
**科目要求**：選修科表現至關重要：選修1中位數為5，選修2中位數為4。中文和英文中位數分別為4和3.5，而公民與社會發展科只需「達標」。
**申請需求**：2025年有180名Band A申請者、80名Band B申請者，總申請人數420人，僅30個一年級學額。Band A與學額比例為6:1，顯示高度選擇性。
**無面試**：課程不設面試，入學純粹基於HKDSE成績。因此，最大化最佳5科成績至關重要，尤其是選修科。
**趨勢**：近年中位數穩定在26-27分左右，顯示競爭力持續。分數高於27分的申請者機會較大，而26分左右的申請者應視為實際目標。

alumni.title: 知名校友
content: **陳家樂博士**：香港環境保護署環境政策顧問。2012年畢業於嶺南大學跨學科課程，以領導城市減廢措施聞名。
**黃佩珊女士**：本地非政府組織「綠色未來香港」聯合創辦人，專注可持續城市農業。2015年畢業，曾獲香港環境卓越獎。
**李偉霆先生**：港鐵公司可持續發展經理。2018年畢業，負責公司的碳中和路線圖，曾入選香港規劃師學會「青年可持續發展領袖」名單。
**劉詩敏博士**：香港大學地理系助理教授。2013年畢業於嶺南大學後取得博士學位，研究沿海社區的氣候變化適應。
**鄭曉琳女士**：聯合國開發計劃署中國辦事處項目主任。2016年畢業，負責農村省份的可持續發展目標實施。
**吳建恒先生**：Eco-Link Consulting創辦人，一家為企業提供ESG報告服務的精品顧問公司。2014年畢業，現任嶺南大學可持續發展學生的導師。

scholarships.title: 獎學金與資助
content: **嶺南大學入學獎學金**：頒予HKDSE成績優異者（最佳5科28分或以上）。涵蓋首年全額或部分學費，並根據學業成績可續領。約10%的新生獲得此獎學金。
**環球可持續發展課程獎學金**：專為JS7123學生而設，要求GPA 3.5或以上。每年提供高達50,000港元，用於學費和學習相關開支。
**交流獎學金**：支持參與海外交流計劃的學生。涵蓋機票、住宿和生活費，每學期高達80,000港元。超過60%的合資格學生獲得資助。
**社區服務獎學金**：頒予在服務研習和社區項目中表現卓越的學生。每年提供20,000港元，並優先獲得國際義工機會。
**香港特區政府獎學金**：適用於學業和課外活動表現出色的本地學生。每年價值40,000港元，另設殘疾學生獎項。
**按需資助**：嶺南大學通過「嶺南大學經濟援助計劃」提供經審查的助學金和貸款。可涵蓋低收入家庭學生的全額學費和生活費。

tips.title: Ace Sir JS7123 攻略 — 9 個實用貼士
content: **1. 優先處理選修科**
- 2025年選修1中位數為5，選修2中位數為4，因此至少一科選修科要達到5級或以上。選擇與可持續發展相關的科目，如地理、經濟或生物。
**2. 目標最佳5科27分或以上**
- 中位數為26.96分，27分或以上可大幅增加優勢。及早計算預測分數，專注改善弱項。
**3. 中文和英文要出色**
- 中文中位數為4，英文中位數為3.5。目標兩科均達4級以保持競爭力。中文練習論說文和閱讀理解；英文注重詞彙和批判分析。
**4. 將公民科視為基本門檻**
- 公民與社會發展科只需「達標」，因此分配最少時間。將節省的時間用於提升選修科成績。
**5. 發揮博雅教育優勢**
- 嶺南大學重視批判性思考和跨學科知識。在個人陳述（如有需要）中，突出你對政策、文化、商業和環境的興趣。
**6. 在JUPAS中及早申請**
- 180名Band A申請者爭奪30個學額，Band A位置至關重要。將JS7123放在Band A的第一或第二志願。
**7. 善用無面試優勢**
- 課程不設面試，HKDSE成績是唯一標準。全力專注考試準備，而非面試練習。
**8. 研究四個專修方向**
- 了解四個專修方向，並相應調整選修科選擇。例如，選擇商業及經濟方向應修讀經濟和企業、會計與財務概論；人類與環境的互動方向則選地理和生物。
**9. 為交流和獎學金做好規劃**
- 目標GPA 3.5或以上，以符合課程獎學金和交流資助資格。及早研究夥伴大學並準備語言要求。

nameEn: Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Animation and Digital Arts
nameZh: 動畫及數碼藝術(榮譽)文學士

curriculum.title: Curriculum Overview
content: **Programme Structure**: The Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Animation and Digital Arts is a 4-year full-time programme under the Faculty of Arts, offering two concentrations: Digital Animation and Arts & Technology. Students choose one concentration in Year 2.

**Year 1 Foundation**: Students take core liberal arts courses (e.g., Critical Thinking, Creativity and Innovation) alongside introductory studio modules like Drawing Fundamentals, Digital Imaging, and Introduction to Animation. Emphasis on building visual literacy and technical basics.

**Year 2 Specialisation**: Students select either Digital Animation (focusing on 2D/3D animation, character design, and storytelling) or Arts & Technology (exploring interactive media, generative art, and digital fabrication). Both streams include a compulsory internship or community project.

**Year 3 Advanced Practice**: Deep-dive into concentration-specific modules: Digital Animation students take Advanced 3D Modelling, Visual Effects, and Animation Production Pipeline; Arts & Technology students study Creative Coding, Immersive Media (VR/AR), and Sound Art. A cross-disciplinary collaborative project is required.

**Year 4 Capstone and Portfolio**: Students complete a Final Year Project (FYP) — a substantial animation or digital art piece — and a Professional Portfolio module. Graduates must present a public exhibition of their work, often held at Lingnan's campus gallery or partner venues.

**Liberal Arts Core**: All students complete the Common Core (36 credits) covering humanities, social sciences, and Chinese/English communication, plus a mandatory residential hall experience and service-learning component.

career.title: Career Prospects
content: **Animation Industry**: Graduates can pursue roles as 2D/3D animators, character designers, storyboard artists, or VFX artists in Hong Kong's growing animation studios (e.g., Imagi Studios, MediaMation) and international production houses.

**Digital Arts and Tech**: The Arts & Technology concentration opens doors to careers in interactive media design, creative coding, VR/AR development, and digital fabrication — skills in demand at tech firms, museums, and advertising agencies.

**Education and Academia**: With a BA (Hons) degree, graduates can teach visual arts or digital media at secondary schools (after completing PGDE) or pursue MPhil/PhD in digital arts, animation studies, or cultural technology.

**Creative Industries**: Alumni find work in film post-production, game design, UI/UX design, and motion graphics for broadcast media. Lingnan's liberal arts training also prepares graduates for roles in arts administration, curation, and cultural policy.

**Entrepreneurship**: The programme's emphasis on portfolio development and project management equips graduates to start their own animation studios, freelance as digital artists, or launch creative tech startups.

**Further Studies**: Many graduates pursue master's degrees in animation, digital media, or arts technology at top institutions worldwide, including Royal College of Art, School of Visual Arts (NYC), and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

campus.title: Campus Life & Facilities
content: **Animation and Digital Arts Studios**: Lingnan's dedicated studios are equipped with industry-standard software (Maya, Blender, Adobe Creative Suite), motion capture systems, and high-performance workstations for rendering and compositing.

**Residential Hall Experience**: All students must live on campus for at least one year, fostering a close-knit community. Halls host creative workshops, film screenings, and animation clubs — ideal for networking and peer learning.

**Tuen Mun Campus**: Located in the New Territories, the campus features modern lecture theatres, a library with extensive digital arts collections, and the Lingnan Gallery for student exhibitions. The scenic seaside setting inspires creativity.

**Exchange and Internship Opportunities**: Lingnan has over 200 partner universities worldwide. JS7133 students can spend a semester abroad at institutions like Tokyo University of the Arts or University of the Arts London, or intern at local animation studios and tech companies.

**Service-Learning and Community Engagement**: The programme integrates community-based projects, such as creating animations for NGOs or teaching digital art to underprivileged youth. This aligns with Lingnan's liberal arts mission of social responsibility.

**Student Societies and Events**: The Animation and Digital Arts Society organises annual showcases, guest lectures by industry professionals (e.g., from Disney, Pixar, local studios), and hackathons. The Lingnan Arts Festival features student films and interactive installations.

competitiveness.title: Competitiveness & Admission Data
content: **Overall Level**: High (★★★★☆)

**Median Score (2025)**: 24.00 (Best 5 subjects), with Lower Quartile at 23.50. This places JS7133 among moderately competitive programmes at Lingnan, requiring strong performance in electives (Median 4 in Elective 1).

**Subject Requirements**: Chinese Language median 4, English median 3, Mathematics median 3, Citizenship & Social Development median Attained. Elective 1 median 4 indicates the programme values depth in one arts/design-related subject.

**Demand and Places**: In 2025 JUPAS cycle, 350 applicants competed for 25 first-year intake places — a ratio of 14:1. Band A applicants numbered 150, showing strong interest from top-choice candidates.

**Interview Required**: All shortlisted candidates must attend an interview (likely portfolio-based). The interview assesses creativity, technical aptitude, and motivation. Preparation is critical — see Tips section.

**Band Preferences**: With 150 Band A applicants and only 25 places, Band A is essential. Band B applicants (70) have limited chances unless their interview performance is exceptional. Band C or below rarely succeed.

alumni.title: Notable Alumni
